title: Practice Exam 1
description: A broad first pass across all five exam objectives.

questions.prompt: Which directory inside a Delta table's storage location contains the transaction log?

options.text: _delta_log
_transaction_log
_checkpoint
_metadata

questions.explanation: Delta Lake records every atomic commit as a JSON file under `_delta_log`, alongside periodic Parquet checkpoint files. That log is what provides ACID guarantees, time travel, and schema enforcement.

questions.prompt: A data engineer schedules a nightly notebook and wants the compute to shut down as soon as the run finishes, with no idle cost. Which compute should they configure?

options.text: A job cluster defined on the scheduled job
An all-purpose cluster shared with the analytics team
An all-purpose cluster with a 10-minute auto-termination window
An instance pool with a minimum idle instance count

questions.explanation: A job cluster is provisioned for a single run and terminated the moment that run completes, so there is no idle period at all. All-purpose clusters stay alive for interactive work — even with auto-termination, they idle until the window elapses.

questions.domain: ELT with Spark SQL and Python
questions.prompt: The statement below runs against an existing Delta table named `sales_summary`. What is the outcome?

code.source:
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE sales_summary AS
SELECT region, sum(amount) AS total
FROM sales
GROUP BY region;

options.text: The table's contents are replaced with the query result, and earlier versions remain available through time travel
The statement fails because the table already exists
The query result is appended to the existing rows
The table is dropped and recreated, permanently discarding its history

questions.explanation: `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` atomically overwrites both data and schema, but on a Delta table this is committed as a new version rather than a drop. Prior versions stay queryable via time travel until they are vacuumed.

questions.domain: ELT with Spark SQL and Python
questions.prompt: The nightly merge below runs against a Delta table. What happens to a row in `updates` whose `user_id` already exists in `users`?

code.source:
MERGE INTO users u
USING updates s
  ON u.user_id = s.user_id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET *
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *;

options.text: Its column values overwrite the matching row in `users`
It is inserted, leaving two rows with the same `user_id`
It is skipped, because `WHEN MATCHED` only applies to deletes
The statement fails on the duplicate key

questions.explanation: `WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET *` updates every column of the target row from the source. `INSERT *` handles only the non-matching rows, so the operation is an upsert and no duplicates are created.

questions.prompt: Which value completes the Auto Loader stream below?

options.text: cloudFiles
autoLoader
delta
json

questions.explanation: Auto Loader is invoked through the `cloudFiles` source. The format of the files being ingested is supplied separately via the `cloudFiles.format` option — here, JSON.

questions.prompt: In Unity Catalog, how is a table addressed by its fully qualified name?

options.text: catalog.schema.table
schema.table
metastore.catalog.table
workspace.schema.table

questions.explanation: Unity Catalog introduces a three-level namespace: catalog, then schema (formerly database), then the object. The older two-level `schema.table` form refers to the default catalog.
